title: Sands
observed_goal: The page text describes a goal of building/growing a desert settlement and cultivating an oasis; active gameplay or a playable objective was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
observed_controls: not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; acceptance of any of the inputs Enter, Space, ArrowUp, w, ArrowRight, or the combination of holding ArrowRight + Space was not confirmed in the frames.
observed_core_loop: not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; the frames show a loading screen with a progress bar and changing messages, not a repeatable game loop.
progress_feedback: The screenshots show a progress bar and stage percentages; the metadata text recorded 4%, 74%, 78%, 79%, and 83% for the stages, respectively. Changes between frames alone do not show that input was accepted and may be caused by animation or the passage of time.
decisions_risk_reward: not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; no playable player decision, risk, choice, or trade-off was seen in the frames.
rewards: The page text mentions a «harmony bonus» after clicking dust devils, but this claim was not confirmed in gameplay/a playable loop.
penalties_failure: not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; no failure, penalty, or error message was seen in the frames.
outcomes_replay: not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; no outcome, win/loss, stage completion, or replay possibility was seen in the frames.
onboarding: The loading screen has a title and subtitle and displays instructional/atmospheric messages; interactive onboarding or a usable start menu was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
visual_audio_accessibility: The screenshots show a full-screen image of an illustrated desert world, the title Sands, a subtitle, a progress bar, and white text on a dark background. Audio was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; the metadata recorded an AudioContext warning. Accessibility features were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
technical_clues: The metadata records two canvases: one 300×150 and the other 1280×800, both with CSS dimensions of 1280×800; this is only a technical clue and does not establish the architecture or role of either canvas.
The metadata records 9 scripts, one stylesheet, 90 images, one XHR, and 8 fetches; the scripts were not scanned, and no engine marker or tuning constant was reported.
The AudioContext warning says that starting audio after a user gesture was not permitted; therefore, the game’s audio state cannot be inferred from this evidence.
A WebGL software-fallback warning and a 403 response were recorded; their relationship to the game logic was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
The metadata explicitly warns that a screenshot change may be animation or the passage of time and is not proof that input was understood.
transferable_principles: Progress should be accompanied by clear visual feedback distinguishable from changes caused solely by time.
Short, staged guidance can introduce the apparent objective without exposing technical details.
To claim that a game loop exists, action, feedback, and a repeatable outcome must be seen across multiple independent frames.
Environmental feedback can create a sense of progress, but it should not be treated as a measurable game outcome.
candle_climber_relevance: For Candle Climber, only the general principles of progress feedback and staged guidance are transferable; these frames do not confirm a control pattern or game loop.
Any score/rank in Candle Climber should reflect skill only, not purchases or a wallet, and should not create an advantage from payment.
Avoid a free brake and horizontal direction changes; a branching path requiring new controls is likewise presented only as a hypothesis requiring testing, not as a conclusion from this game.
Any potential adaptation should remain abstract and should not reproduce this game’s name, characters, art, level, text, audio, brand, or assets.
do_not_copy: Do not reproduce any specific name, character, art, level, text, audio, brand, or asset from this game.
Do not copy/interpret the increase in percentage between frames as causation by input or proof of a game loop.
Do not turn the official card’s claim about building a settlement, water channels, gardens, or postcard-perfect moments into a definite mechanic without playtesting.

evidence.claim: The load frame shows a loading screen with the title Sands, the subtitle A DESERT DIORAMA, a progress bar, and the text Raising the dunes.
In the after_start frame, the same loading screen shows the text Dust devils wander the basin. Click one for a harmony bonus. and 74%.
The page text for the after_key_burst stage records 78% and guidance to click dust devils for a harmony bonus.
The page text for the after_combined_input stage records 79%; this change alone does not establish acceptance of the combined input.
The late frame shows the message After a sandstorm, spice blooms break through the sand. and a progress bar at approximately 84%; no game outcome or complete loop was observed.
The official game card presents it as an experience of shaping a desert settlement, arranging architecture, directing water to gardens, and discovering picturesque moments.
The metadata records a screenshot change but cautions that it may be caused by animation or the passage of time and is not proof that input was understood.
The console recorded an AudioContext warning, a WebGL software fallback, and a 403 response; their effect on the game logic was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.

limitations: All evidence is limited to the loading screen and recorded metadata. No observable active gameplay, accepted control, repeatable loop, outcome, win/loss, or clear game menu was seen. The percentage figures in the metadata text differ slightly from the readable percentages in some screenshots; therefore, they were used only as recorded loading feedback. No web browsing was performed, and no files outside this game’s inputs were used.
